newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: Joint Anglo-Argentine oil licences seen by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Joint Anglo-Argentine oil licences seen by 1998.

text.p: Licences for oil exploration in joint Anglo-Argentine territory southwest of the Falkland Islands known as the "Special Cooperation Area" could be issued earlier than expected, according to the islands' director of oil.

Phyllis Rendell said the licences, which would be issued by the joint Anglo-Argentine South West Atlantic Hydrocarbons Commission (SWAHC), could be allocated by 1998 -- two years earlier than expected.
The islands' former director of oil, John Martin, said on Wednesday oil exploration licensing for the "Special Cooperation Area" risked being delayed by bureaucratic wrangling on the part of SWAHC.
"They have to marry two taxes, two sets of environmental regulations, two sets of operation regulations... and I don't know when it will be issued.
"They talk about within the next two years, but I think that's very optimistic because it's only now that they have agreed an agenda of what to talk about," he said.
SWAHC, which is controlled by the British and Argentine governments with minimum input from the Falkland Islands government, is due to meet in London on December 9 and 10.

Despite Buenos Aires constitutional claim to the islands, Britain and Argentina restored diplomatic links in 1989 and last year signed an agreement on the framework for oil and gas exploration in the "Special Cooperation Area," which straddles the median line between the Islands and the Argentine mainland.

Meanwhile, oil exploration in Falkland waters was due to start by the end of the 1996, following the award of permits to 12 companies on October 28 by the islands' government in its first licensing round.
At least two research ships were expected by the end of December and a third by the middle of January.

"The tranches in the south part of the northern area are affected by a fisheries conservation ban which becomes effective on March 1, hence the rush," said Nigel Fannin of the British Geological Survey, the Falkland Government's oil consultants.
Fannin said drilling for oil in Falklands waters could commence as early as the austral summer of 1997-98.

"The seismic data which the companies will obtain at the beginning of 1997 will take six months to assess which will then give them an opportunity to exactly site the well which they will drill," he said.
